abstract.p: Medical image diagnosis inherently involves uncertainty due to artifacts, occlusions, and ambiguous visual patterns, often leading to high inter-observer variability. While deep neural networks offer strong predictive performance, their outputs tend to be overconfident and poorly calibrated, limiting their clinical reliability. We propose Conformal Focal Loss (CFL), a principled approach that leverages the focal loss and the statistical validity of conformal prediction to better characterize diagnostic uncertainty. By emphasizing hard or ambiguous examples, CFL enables more accurate estimation of both predictive confidence and ambiguity. We evaluate CFL on diagnostic tasks using both clean and noise-augmented datasets, demonstrating its ability to effectively identify uncertain cases while maintaining robust classification performance under label noise.
